theme: Steven Bonta partial decipherment, distributional fields, lexical chance and ICIT source history
question: Do Bonta's structural observations reproduce on pinned corpora, do identifiable anchor readings exceed a fixed lexical chance model, and is the claimed ICIT check demonstrably reserved at object level?
outcome: On 2469 selected objects jar 740 is final 838/1196 (70.07%) and arrow 520 is final 192/225 (85.33%). Elementary fish runs: 757, zero repeats and zero longer than three. Six-role ten-type lexical panel: 9/10 matches; normalized tail 13/720=0.0180556, exact-among-variants tail 3/720=0.0041667. Prefix intersection: 35 candidate classes. These condition on Bonta-selected developmental examples. Manual source-history audit confirms three repeated catalogue objects among six parser candidates, rejects two and marks one conflict; the claimed 12–15 validation set and attempt/failure denominators remain unknown. Zero usable physical-quantity joins. 126 scoped claim records and 17 candidate mappings; complete field and reading replication remain unfinished.
challenge: Full manuscript glyphs/figures absent, historical ICIT frame and development timestamps missing, fine allograph mappings uncertain, conditional lexical rule narrower than discretionary author matching, and no inscription-to-measured-quantity join. Direct Academia requests fail 403 and Nature 200 responses are interstitial HTML.
remedy: Preserved the pre-outcome protocol, fixed a six-role panel using the introductory-letter images, used object-grouped counts and all 720 value permutations, retained all original outcomes, manually audited parser overlaps in a separate output, documented failed access and incomplete coverage, and verified an identical replay with 54/54 independent checks.
retry_when: Obtain the full 2024 manuscript images and first-edition witness, source-qualified fine sign mappings and field boundaries, the historical ICIT validation list with attempted/rejected readings and pre-check values, or an independently measured quantity tied to an inscription. Freeze acceptance rules and reserve objects before a larger lexical test.
